ov: An extinct flightless bird of Mauritius, in the Indian Ocean, in the pigeon and dove family; its closest living relative is the Nicobar pigeon. It stood about 63–75 cm tall and probably ate fruit. Hunting and introduced animals wiped it out by the 1660s.

why.et: Sailors ate it, though early Dutch accounts do not agree on how good it tasted.

df: Probably fruit; it swallowed stones to help digest food.
fx: What it looked like is known only from 17th-century drawings, paintings and written accounts.
Its extinction went unnoticed at first, and some people later thought it was a myth.
notes: The animals.js fact is confirmed: first recorded by Dutch sailors in 1598, last widely accepted sighting 1662; it was in the pigeon family.
